sections.h2: Where do I take a deed to be recorded in Shelby County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Take it to the Shelby County Recorder on the second floor of the county annex at 129 E. Court Street in Sidney. The office phone is 937-498-7270 and the fax is 937-498-7272. Recording closes a little before the business day does: the office is open to the public Monday through Thursday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but it accepts documents for recording only until 4:15 p.m. On Friday it keeps business hours until noon and takes recordings until 11:45 a.m.

The Recorder's page calls the office the steward of the county's real estate records and says they reach back to the county's start, when the land was still part of Miami County. The online index covers July 1, 1989 forward. Older research means a trip to the office, and staff will help, though they do not do genealogy searches for outsiders.

Sidney is the only city in the county, and the rest of Shelby County is villages, townships and farmland. A deed here may describe a Sidney street lot, a village house in a place with German roots, or acreage along the Great Miami River.

sections.h2: What does Shelby County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Shelby County's 2025 fee schedule sets the price of a deed, mortgage or lease at $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that. The schedule says fees rose by $5 on January 1, 2025, because Senate Bill 94 allows a preservation and digitization surcharge, and ORC 317.32 now caps that surcharge at five dollars per instrument.

Shelby County Recorder charges on the 2025 schedule
ServiceCharge
Deed, mortgage, lease, most documents$39 for pages one and two
Pages beyond two, with attachments$8 each
Marginal notation$4 each
Document that misses the standard format$20
Plat, 11 by 17 inches$40
Plat, 24 by 36 inches$86
UCC financing statement$12 plus $4 per name indexed

The county's own FAQ adds a warning: documents with the wrong fee, short or over, come back unrecorded. Count the pages and include the exact total with the deed.

sections.h2: What do Shelby County recorder staff look for in a deed?
sections.html:
The Recorder's fee page lists the rules plainly:

  • Every document needs a legal description, and it must read as it does on the prior deed. A description with missing parts is rejected.
  • Mail filings need a self-addressed stamped envelope. Without postage for the return, the office holds the document.
  • Marginal notations require the volume and page of the earlier record, and each one adds $4.
  • An affidavit has to say who the current owner of the property is.

State law adds the signature step. ORC 5301.01 requires the grantor to sign and to acknowledge the signature before a judge, clerk of a court of record, county auditor, county engineer, notary or mayor. A deed that skips the acknowledgment is not ready to record.

The Recorder may also decline certain items. ORC 317.13 says the recorder must refuse a right-to-list home sale agreement and may refuse an instrument that the Revised Code does not require or authorize to be recorded. The county page carries a public notice that deed language limiting a home's sale, rental or use by race, color, sex, religion, national origin, handicap or familial status is invalid under the federal Fair Housing Act.

sections.h2: Who collects the Shelby County conveyance fee?
sections.html:
The Shelby County Auditor does, before the Recorder files anything. The Auditor's transfer fee page prints the real estate transfer fee as $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus $.50 per parcel. The Auditor's site also offers a calculation form for the conveyance and transfer fee.

Two statutes sit behind that number. ORC 319.54(G)(3) imposes the base charge of one dollar or ten cents per hundred, whichever is more, and ORC 322.02 authorizes commissioners to add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per hundred. The seller is the grantor, and the statute puts the transfer tax on the grantor, so the seller pays at the time the deed is delivered.

Not every transfer owes it. Gifts within a family, deeds to correct an earlier deed, transfers into a revocable trust and transfers between heirs with no money paid are listed exemptions. Whether yours qualifies is a question for the Auditor.

sections.h2: What is the land like in Shelby County?
sections.html:
Shelby County sits in western Ohio and covers 411 square miles, with 408 of them land. Wikipedia describes low rolling hills, almost all of it farmed or built up. The Great Miami River enters from Logan County near the middle and leaves into Miami County. The highest ground, 1,149 feet, lies in the southeast corner where Champaign and Miami counties meet it.

The 2020 census counted 48,230 residents, with about 43 percent in urban areas. The county's first seat of government was Hardin, named for a pioneer killed there in 1792, before Sidney took over. When the county was cut down in 1848, Minster and New Bremen moved into the new Auglaize County. Many Shelby County towns trace to German immigrants, and the Miami and Erie Canal, which reached the county in 1841, gave those newcomers early work.

For a seller, the geography means plenty of rural parcels. A farmhouse on a few acres may need a survey or a split approved before it can be deeded separately, so ask the Auditor's office early about description rules.

sections.h2: How do Shelby County property tax records and relief programs work?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate section covers valuation and tax rates, revaluation information, owner occupancy and homestead tax reductions, delinquent payment plans and razed or damaged structures. A seller can search a parcel there to see the value on record before listing.

  • Value disputes start with a complaint to the county Board of Revision, which under ORC 5715.19 takes complaints through March 31 of the following year, or the close of first-half collection if that is later.
  • State homestead rules for 2026 set a $29,700 reduction for seniors and the disabled and a $41,000 income limit, with applications due December 31 of the year sought, according to the Ohio Department of Taxation.
  • Back taxes can sometimes be paid through a delinquent payment plan, which the Auditor's menu lists. Ask there for terms.

At closing the title agent requests the tax payoff from the county. Because Ohio bills real estate in two halves, the amount owed depends on when in the year the sale closes.

faqs.q: What are the Shelby County Recorder's hours for recording a deed?
faqs.a: Monday through Thursday, recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., and Friday it runs 8:30 to 11:45 a.m. General business hours go slightly later, to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and noon on Friday, according to the Recorder's page.

faqs.q: How much is the Shelby County recording fee for a two-page deed?
faqs.a: $39, based on the 2025 fee schedule: $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after. A non-standard document adds $20 and each marginal notation adds $4.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder hold my deed if I mail it?
faqs.a: Yes, if you leave out the return envelope. The county asks for a self-addressed stamped envelope with mailed documents and holds the deed until postage is supplied. A wrong fee also stops the recording.

faqs.q: What is the Shelby County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor prints $4 per $1,000 of sale price plus $.50 per parcel. The Auditor collects it before the deed goes to the Recorder, and exempt transfers file an exemption form instead.

faqs.q: Can I search Shelby County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Partly. The Recorder's website offers the index from July 1, 1989 forward. Earlier records are in the office, and staff can help you in person, but they decline genealogical research requests.
